$comment: Charter filings: Certificate of Formation (LLC) and Certificate of Incorporation (C-Corp). These are the public documents filed with the Secretary of State, so they stay deliberately thin — everything negotiable belongs in the governance document, which is not public.

clauses.title: Name
clauses.rationale: Statutorily required in every state. The name must exactly match the availability check.

clauses.title: Purpose
clauses.rationale: A general-purpose clause avoids having to amend the charter when the business changes direction.
clauses.body: The Company is organized to engage in any lawful act or activity for which a {{entityLong}} may be organized under the laws of {{formStateLong}}, including without limitation the business of {{industryName}}.

clauses.title: Registered Office and Agent
clauses.rationale: Every state requires an in-state agent for service of process. Using a founder's home address makes that address public and permanent.
clauses.body: The address of the Company’s registered office in {{formStateLong}} is {{agentAddress}}, and the name of its [[registered agent]] at that address is {{agent}}.

clauses.title: Organizer
clauses.rationale: The organizer signs the filing. They need not be a Member, and their role ends when the Company is formed.
clauses.body: The name and address of the organizer executing this {{charterDoc}} is {{founder1}}, whose authority terminates upon the filing of this document and the admission of the initial {{ownerTerm}} under <<xr:consent_adopt>>.

clauses.title: Incorporator
clauses.rationale: The incorporator appoints the initial board and then resigns. Skipping the resignation leaves an ambiguous authority in the record.
clauses.body: The name and address of the incorporator is {{founder1}}. The powers of the incorporator terminate upon the appointment of the initial directors under <<xr:consent_adopt>>.

clauses.title: Management
clauses.rationale: Several states require the charter to state whether the LLC is member-managed or manager-managed.
clauses.body: The Company shall be {{mgmtStyle}}. The rights and obligations of the {{ownerTerm}} are set forth in the [[Operating Agreement|operating agreement]] referenced in <<xr:gov_formation>>.

clauses.title: Authorized Stock
clauses.rationale: Authorized share count and par value drive Delaware franchise tax under the authorized-shares method, so the numbers are not cosmetic.
clauses.body: The Company is authorized to issue {{authShares}} shares of Common Stock, [[par value]] {{parValue}} per share. The number of [[authorized shares]] may be increased only by amendment of this {{charterDoc}}.

clauses.title: Blank Check Preferred
clauses.benchmark: Present in 81% of venture-track certificates of incorporation
clauses.rationale: Lets the board designate a preferred series at closing without a separate stockholder vote, which removes a step from every financing.
clauses.body: The Board is authorized to designate one or more series of [[Preferred Stock|preferred stock]] and to fix the rights, preferences, and limitations of each series by resolution, without further action by the {{ownerTerm}}.

clauses.title: Limitation of Director Liability
clauses.benchmark: Present in 94% of Delaware certificates of incorporation
clauses.rationale: Exculpation must appear in the charter to be effective; putting it only in the bylaws does not work.
clauses.body: To the fullest extent permitted by law, no director shall be personally liable to the Company or its {{ownerTerm}} for monetary damages for breach of [[fiduciary duty]] as a director. No amendment to this provision shall reduce the protection of a director for any act occurring before the amendment.

clauses.title: Charter-Level Indemnification
clauses.rationale: Bylaw indemnification can be amended by a later board. Charter-level indemnification cannot be removed without a stockholder vote, which is what an outside director actually wants to see.
clauses.body: The Company shall indemnify its directors and officers to the fullest extent permitted by law, and this right shall not be eliminated or impaired by any amendment to this {{charterDoc}} with respect to acts occurring before the amendment.

clauses.title: Duration
clauses.rationale: Perpetual existence is the default in every state in this library. The clause is included for readers who expect to see it.
clauses.body: The Company shall have perpetual existence unless dissolved in accordance with <<xr:gov_dissolution>>.
